title: Refund Authority Threshold Change with Undocumented Grace Period
scenario_text:
Google Workspace — 'Return & Refund Policy RP-2026-v1' (Published Feb 1, 2026)
Section 4.2: 'Refund-without-receipt transactions exceeding $100 require Loss Prevention Manager approval. Store managers may approve refunds without receipt up to $100.'
Section 4.2 (Footnote): 'Replaces RP-2025-v3 Section 4.1, effective immediately upon publication.'

Google Workspace — 'Return & Refund Policy RP-2025-v3' (Archived Jan 31, 2026)
Section 4.1: 'Refund-without-receipt transactions exceeding $300 require LP Director approval. Store managers may approve refunds without receipt up to $300.'

Slack — #store-managers (Feb 1, 2026, 8:02 AM)
@corporate.ops: Team — new return policy RP-2026-v1 is live today. Key change: refund w/o receipt threshold dropped from $300 to $100 for manager-level authority. Please review and confirm.
[14 of 47 managers reacted with checkmark emoji]
[No further replies in thread]

Slack — #store-managers (Feb 3, 2026, 11:15 AM)
@rachel.nguyen: Quick q — I have a customer in-store right now with a $180 return, no receipt. Under the old policy I could approve this. Are we really enforcing the new limit starting today?
@corporate.ops: Policy is effective as of 2/1. Please follow the new threshold.
@sandra.lowell: @rachel.nguyen just call LP, they're turning these around in under 5 min
@rachel.nguyen: Got it, thanks

Slack — DM between Anthony DiMaggio and VP of Retail Ops, Karen Marsh (Feb 1, 2026, 10:22 AM)
@karen.marsh: Anthony — heads up, we're going to get a flood of calls on the new $100 limit. Can you give managers a soft 2-week grace period to adjust? Don't formally flag anyone processing between $100-$300 until Feb 15.
@anthony.dimaggio: Makes sense. I'll tell my team to note but not escalate until the 15th.
@karen.marsh: Perfect. Don't put that in writing anywhere official though — I don't want it as a documented exception.

Square POS — Exception Report (UrbanEdge, 5 locations, Feb 1-14, 2026)
23 refund-without-receipt transactions between $100-$300 approved by store managers during this window. None escalated to LP.

Square POS — Exception Report (UrbanEdge, Midtown location, Feb 18, 2026)
Alert: Manager Sandra L. processed refund-without-receipt for $245. Customer: 'T. Whittaker'. No LP approval on file.

Google Sheets — 'LP Exception Log Q1 2026'
Row 12: Date: 2/18 | Brand: UrbanEdge | Location: Midtown | Flag: 'Refund w/o receipt $245, no LP approval' | Manager: Sandra L. | Status: 'Pending review' | Notes: [empty]

Zendesk — Ticket #ZD-438201 (Feb 18, 2026)
Customer: T. Whittaker | Subject: 'Refund issue in store'
Agent note (internal): 'Customer states manager approved refund but it was reversed the next day. Customer upset. Manager Sandra L. says she thought the old policy still applied.'
question: Sandra L. processed a $245 refund-without-receipt on Feb 18 without LP approval. How should this be adjudicated?

contributor.name: Anthony DiMaggio
contributor.title: Loss Prevention Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Return fraud detection, ORC analysis, POS exception monitoring across multi-brand retail

choices: Inconclusive — the grace period was never formally documented, creating ambiguity about whether it constitutes a policy modification; escalate to Legal/HR for interpretation before taking action
No violation — Sandra's claim that she didn't see the policy update is supported by the fact that only 14 of 47 managers acknowledged the Slack announcement, suggesting insufficient notice

Clear policy violation — RP-2026-v1 took effect Feb 1, the published policy requires LP approval over $100, the grace period ended Feb 15, and Sandra processed this transaction on Feb 18; she must be formally flagged

No violation — the informal grace period communicated by the VP of Retail Ops via DM to Anthony extends manager authority to $300 through at least Feb 15, and a reasonable interpretation allows additional adjustment time
